paragraphs.text: Though scattered among the heathen, and in a sorrowful condition, Psa 106:47. In prosperity praise the Lord, saith Austin, and it shall increase upon thee. In adversity praise him, and it shall be better with thee.
paragraphs.anchor: Praise ye the Lord

paragraphs.text: This verse was, say some, the foot or tenor of the song in many sacred hymns.
paragraphs.anchor: O give thanks unto the Lord, &c.

paragraphs.text: Even to those also that have sinned against his goodness.
paragraphs.anchor: For his mercy endureth for ever

paragraphs.text: i.e. To the just worth of them; none can: they are fitter to be admired than possible to be uttered. It is enough that we do what we can toward the work. God accepteth according to that a man hath, and not according to that he hath not, 2Co 8:12; he taketh it for no small praise when we thus acknowledge him to be above all praise.
paragraphs.anchor: Who can utter, &c.

paragraphs.text: Quis fando exprimat? Surely none can. David saith he will, Psa 9:1, but soon found his utter inability; for according to thy name, O Lord, so is thy praise, saith he in another psalm. The best way is, as here in the ensuing verses, to submit to God’s justice, and to implore his mercy, and to study integrity, Psa 106:3-6.
paragraphs.anchor: Who can show forth all his praise?

paragraphs.text: That are of right principles and upright practices; this is real and substantial praising of God. Thanks doing is the proof of thanksgiving; and the good life of the thankful is the life of thankfulness. Those that say God a-thank only, and no more, are not only contumelious, but injurious.
paragraphs.anchor: Blessed are they that keep judgment, &c.

paragraphs.text: So preaching forth the virtues (or praises) of God who hath called him into his marvellous light, 1Pe 2:9, and composing his whole course, velar spectatum aliquod simulaehrum et documentum laudis eius constans atque perpetuum (Jun.).
paragraphs.anchor: And he that doth righteousness

paragraphs.text: The psalmist would have favour, and special favour, mercies, and sure mercies, proper to God’s peculiar, and with these he would be remembered; grace he would find, such as might help in time of need, Heb 4:16. "God remembered Noah," Gen 8:1. "Your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of these things," Mat 6:32. Though our ark be driven in a tempestuous sea, yet it shall neither sink nor split while we sail in the thoughts of God.
paragraphs.anchor: Remember me, O Lord, with the favour, &c.

paragraphs.text: A gracious spirit will not be satisfied with low things, common mercies,
paragraphs.anchor: O visit me with thy salvation

paragraphs.text: Ut videam in bonum, that I may see it, and partake of it, have both the vision and fruition of thy great goodness, which thou hast laid up for them that fear thee, Psa 31:19, giving them a taste thereof aforehand, as a few grapes of that promised Canaan.
paragraphs.anchor: That I may see the good of thy chosen

paragraphs.text: i.e. By this name God’s elect are here and elsewhere styled, and therefore the Jews have no reason to reproach us, as they do, by it; calling us Gel, and Mamzer-goi, bastard heathens.
paragraphs.anchor: Of thy nation

paragraphs.text: Adding to their heap, and making up their measure, Mat 23:32. People think the example of their fathers a sufficient excuse. Jerome once (but not well) desired leave of Austin to err with seven Fathers whom he found of his opinion. I will follow my forefathers, saith Cicero, although I fall together with them. See Jer 44:17. But so would not these good souls, as neither Jeremiah, Jer 3:25, nor Daniel, Dan 9:5, whose confession suiting and symbolizing with this (together with that we read Psa 106:47), maketh some think that this psalm was penned for his people’s use then when they were captives in Babylon.
paragraphs.anchor: We have sinned with our fathers

paragraphs.text: Sin must be confessed with utmost aggravation. I will hear how full in the mouth these are against themselves, laying on load, while their sins swell as so many toads in their eyes.
paragraphs.anchor: We have committed iniquity, &c.

paragraphs.text: i.e. They weighed them not, improved them not, but as the dull earth is surrounded by the heavens, yet perceiveth it not; so were these with miracles and mercies, yet understood them not.
paragraphs.anchor: Our fathers understood not

paragraphs.text: Not only while they were on the bank they feared to enter, but also even when they were passing and walking over that dry land made for them by a miracle, they did still continue their murmurings and mutinings.
paragraphs.anchor: Even at the Red Sea

paragraphs.text: Nevertheless he saved them for his name’s sake] Here he comes, in with a Non-obstante. So Isa 57:17. Now, if God will save for his name’s sake, what people is there whom he may not save?
The Lord hath other things to look unto than presently to punish his people when they most deserve it.
paragraphs.anchor: That he might make his miqhly power to be known

paragraphs.text: Ingentia beneficia, flagitia, supplicia, as appeareth in the subsequent verses.
paragraphs.anchor: He rebuked the Red Sea also

paragraphs.text: Inter duas aquarum congeries, between two mountains of waters, which stood on each hand of them as a wall, and made a lane. Every main affliction is our Red Sea; which while it threateneth to swallow us up, preserveth us.
paragraphs.anchor: So he led them through the depths

paragraphs.text: From Pharaoh, that perfect enemy of theirs, that pursued them with a deadly design, but was happily prevented.
paragraphs.anchor: And he saved them, &c.

paragraphs.text: The preservation of the Church is ever accompanied with the destruction of its enemies, that the mercy may appear the greater.
paragraphs.anchor: And the waters covered their enemies

paragraphs.text: Left alive to carry the news.
paragraphs.anchor: Not one of them left

paragraphs.text: Then for a flash, while the memory of the mercy was fresh and warm; but ere they were three days older they murmured again; it proved not so much as a nine days’ wonderment; they were soon at oldward.
paragraphs.anchor: Then believed they his words

paragraphs.text: Exo 15:1-21 A temporary faith and joy.
paragraphs.anchor: They sang his praise

paragraphs.text: Heb. They made haste, they forgat. This is an aggravating circumstance. See Gal 1:6 Exo 32:8 Deu 9:16.
paragraphs.anchor: They soon forgat his works

paragraphs.text: For the performance of what he had purposed and promised; they were short-spirited and impatient.
paragraphs.anchor: They waited not for his counsel

paragraphs.text: Heb. lusted a lust. See Num 11:1-35, they had a sufficiency, but must have superfluities, as belly-gods; not want, but wantonness, set them a lusting, and that in the wilderness, where they knew that in an ordinary way it was not to be had.
paragraphs.anchor: But lusted exceedingly

paragraphs.text: Whom they should have trusted rather, since he waiteth to be gracious, and being a God of judgment, knoweth best when to deal forth his favours, Isa 30:18; Isa 49:8.
paragraphs.anchor: And tempted God

paragraphs.text: Deus saepe dat iratus quod negat propitius (Aug.).
paragraphs.anchor: And he gave them their request

paragraphs.text: Munera magna quidem misit, sed misit in hamo
(Martial).
Quails they had, but to choke them; as afterwards a king, but to vex them, &c.

i.e. Into their bodies, such a loathing as caused leanness, Num 11:20, a plague upon their bodies, a curse upon their souls. Many men eat that on earth which they digest in hell. It is dangerous feeding on sin’s murdering morsels.
paragraphs.anchor: But sent leanness into their soul

paragraphs.text: Korah and his complices did; and because the people punished them not, they are all accused as guilty of that conspiracy, and looked upon as a rabble of rebels against heaven.
paragraphs.anchor: They envied Moses also

paragraphs.text: Separated to the priesthood. The Rabbis tell us that they bad chosen Dathan instead of Moses, and Abiram for Aaron.
paragraphs.anchor: And Aaron the saint of the Lord

paragraphs.text: Korah is not here mentioned, haply for his sons’ sakes, who were famous prophets and music masters in David’s days. As for On the son of Peleth (one of the chief conspirators), the Rabbis say that by the good counsel of his wife he repented, and so escaped.
paragraphs.anchor: The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan, &c.

paragraphs.text: It is both a just presage and desert of ruin not to be warned. Let seditious persons and schismatics take heed; for even our God also is a consuming fire, Heb 12:29.
paragraphs.anchor: And a fire was kindled in their company

paragraphs.text: And among the rest Korah, as some conceive. Dathan and Abiram are stigmatized for their stubbornness, Num 26:9, as was afterwards Ahaz, 2Ch 28:22, and before them all Cain, Gen 4:15, and Lamech, Gen 4:24.
paragraphs.anchor: The flame burnt up the wicked

paragraphs.text: i.e. In the country near to that mountain, where they at same time saw visible tokens of God’s dreadful presence. Well might Aaron say of this people, that they were wholly set upon wickedness, Exo 32:22. This piece of idolatry they had learned belike of the Egyptians, who worshipped Apis in such a shape, so catching is sin, and so dangerous is ill company (Lege Lacrant. and Aug. lib. 1, de Mirab. Script. cap. 15).
paragraphs.anchor: They made a calf in Horeb

paragraphs.text: i.e. Their God, Rom 1:23, the Creator for a contemptible creature.
paragraphs.anchor: Thus they changed their glory

paragraphs.text: Tunc stercora egerit, et multum inquinatur, as R. Solomon here glosseth. They pretended not to worship the calf, but God in the calf, as did also Jebu, 2Ki 10:16; 2Ki 10:29 2Ch 11:15, and as the idolatrous Papists do at this day. See Exo 32:5-6. Yet the text here saith, "They worshipped the molten image, they changed their glory into the similitude of an ox." And although some of the Rabbis would excuse this gross idolatry of their forefathers, yet others, more wise, bewail it, and say that there is an ounce of this golden calf in all their present sufferings.
paragraphs.anchor: Of an ox that eateth grass

paragraphs.text: This is often mentioned as the mother of all the misrule among them.
paragraphs.anchor: They forgat God their saviour

paragraphs.text: i.e. Among the Egyptians, Ham’s posterity.
paragraphs.anchor: Wondrous works in the land of Ham

paragraphs.text: All which were buried, together with the remembrance of God, the doer.
paragraphs.anchor: And terrible things by the Red Sea

paragraphs.text: Idolatry is a people desolating sin. God was once in a mind to have destroyed this people utterly, and to have left none but Moses, Exo 32:10; Exo 32:31, &c., promising him a great fortune if he would have suffered it; but he, tendering God’s glory more than his own greatness, refused it: choice and excellent spirits use to do so.
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore he said that he would destroy them

paragraphs.text: "Chosen" to represent Christ in his mediatorship.
paragraphs.anchor: Had not Moses his chosen

paragraphs.text: A metaphor from military matters. When a stronghold is besieged, and a breach made, valiant soldiers use to make up that breach with their own bodies, till the enemy be beaten back. God’s wrath was even breaking in upon the people. Moses prayed instantly and constantly, even the most part of those forty days and nights he spent in the mount, Deu 9:9; Deu 9:11; Deu 9:18; Deu 9:25, and at length prevailed. See Eze 13:5; Eze 22:30.
paragraphs.anchor: Stood up in the breach

paragraphs.text: Heb. The land of desire, flowing with milk and honey, sumen totius terrae, as one calleth it; Egypt they preferred before it, though it were a gage of heaven; as Cardinal Bourbon did his part in Paris, before his part in paradise.
paragraphs.anchor: Yea, they despised the pleasant land

paragraphs.text: sc. That he would, or indeed could, give them that good land. He that believeth not maketh God a liar.
paragraphs.anchor: They believed not his word

paragraphs.text: Where they sat discontented (after the report of the spies), and, as we say, sick of the sullens; they would not attempt a conquest, but bewailed their hard fortune, and let fly on all hands, keeping a clutter and a rattle.
paragraphs.anchor: But murmured in their tents

paragraphs.text: i.e. He solemnly swore, as Num 14:30, or he was fetching his full blow at them.
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore he lifted up his hand

paragraphs.text: Which also befell them according to their own wicked wish. Let men false heed of wishing evil to themselves, lest God say Amen to it.
paragraphs.anchor: To overthrow them in the wilderness

paragraphs.text: This clause of God’s oath is not expressed in Numbers, but drawn there hence as a fearful consequence, both here by the psalmist, and also by the prophet Ezekiel, Eze 20:1-49 And R. Solomon’s note upon this text is, Tunc erat decretum de desolando Templo, ut lachrymas pro re magna, sicut ante pro nihilo effunderent, Then was the desolation of the temple (though it fell out long after) determined, that those malcontents who cried for nothing before, might have somewhat to cry for.
paragraphs.anchor: To overthrow their seed also among the nations

paragraphs.text: Heb. they were unequally yoked, as 2Co 6:14.
paragraphs.anchor: They joined themselves also unto Baalpeor

paragraphs.text: Quam male inaequales veniunt ad aratra iuvenci.
They separated themselves to that shame, Priapus, Hos 9:10, who had his name from showing all, Ab operatione seu nudatione pudendorum; and his worshippers were most impudent servants.

i.e. Of idols opposed to the living God. The beginning of idolatry, some say, was the attributing of divine honours to great persons when they were dead. The heathens showed the sepulchres of their oldest deities.
paragraphs.anchor: And ate the sacrifices of the dead

paragraphs.text: God cannot brook men’s devices in matters of religion; he will have no other worship than what himself hath appointed.
paragraphs.anchor: Thus they provoked him

paragraphs.text: As a deluge, or as an army, very impetuously, to the destroying of twenty-four thousand persons.
paragraphs.anchor: And the plague brake in upon them

paragraphs.text: Animose surrexit (Vatab.). By a secret, heroical, and extraordinary motion of God’s Spirit, such as may not be drawn into example. All things reported and commended in Scripture may not be imitated. One Birchet, by example of Phinehas and Ehud, thought he might have killed a great personage in this land, whom he looked upon as a naughty man, and God’s enemy. A particular example will afford a general instruction, when the equity of the thing done is universal, and the cause common, otherwise not, saith learned Junius.
paragraphs.anchor: Then stood up Phinehas

paragraphs.text: Not tarrying for the sentence of the judges. The Chaldee rendereth it, And prayed. Execution of justice is that actual, magisterial, and majestical kind of prayer that will stay the plague when nothing else will.
paragraphs.anchor: And executed judyment

paragraphs.text: God not only condemned him not of rash zeal, but looked upon what he had done as a piece of singular service, and rewarded it accordingly.
paragraphs.anchor: And that was counted unto him for righteousness

paragraphs.text: Yet he made not the least semblance of it to Moses, but only bade him smite the rock, which, if he had then done, and no more, he had done right. God is Bagnal Chemah, master of his anger, Nah 1:2, so was not meek Moses at this time. The best are miscarried by their passions sometimes, to their cost.
paragraphs.anchor: They angered him also at the waters of strife

paragraphs.text: i.e. By their means he was kept out of Canaan, which was a great cross to him, and his repentance, as to that favour, came too late, for God was resolved.
paragraphs.anchor: So that it went ill with Moses for their sakes

paragraphs.text: So that he was in a pelt to the grieving of God’s good Spirit within him, Eph 4:30-31. O tantaene animis coelestibus irae?
paragraphs.anchor: Because they provoked his spirit

paragraphs.text: Some render it only, he spake, or he pronounced; he should not have spoken at all to the people, as having no order from God so to do in that transaction, but only to the rock. Whereas he not only smote the rock, and smote it twice, but spake to the people, and spake rashly, or idly (the Greek word βαττολογεω is thought to come from the Hebrew Bata here used), yea, bitterly, calling them rebels, and falling foul upon them with distrustful interrogations and misimplications, Et perperam locutus est. Contra charitas, ου περπερευεται, 1Co 13:4. This is called rebellion, Num 20:10-11; Num 20:24, and severely punished in God’s favourite Moses.
paragraphs.anchor: So that he spake unadvisedly

paragraphs.text: For which neglect of theirs pity would be pleaded. But there is a cruel mercy, saith one; there is a pious cruelty, saith another. Cursed is he that doeth the Lord’s work deceitfully, and cursed is he that restraineth his sword from blood when God biddeth him strike. Saul and Ahab felt the dint of this curse, and so did these Israelites, for sparing the Canaanites, whether out of pusillanimity or foolish pity.
paragraphs.anchor: They did not destroy the nations

paragraphs.text: With whom they made leagues and marriages, Jdg 1:3, and so were soon corrupted by them. It is dangerous to converse with graceless people, their very example is a compulsion; see Gal 2:14; how much more their evil counsel!
paragraphs.anchor: But were mingled among the heathen

paragraphs.text: The devil is ειδωλοχαρης, saith Synesius, a lover of idolatry, and he speaks through idolaters as through his trunks, persuading people to like practice, as did Julian, whom an ancient, therefore, called Idolian.
paragraphs.anchor: And they served their idols

paragraphs.text: Or, a ruin, as some render it; they were first drawn in, and then undone by them.
paragraphs.anchor: Which were a snare unto them

paragraphs.text: The devils are here called Shedim, destroyers (in opposition to Shaddai, the Almighty), and worthily; for they make it their work to waste and spoil people of their dearest children, as here, of their precious souls, with the blood whereof they do daily glut themselves.
paragraphs.anchor: Yea, they sacrificed their sons, &c.

paragraphs.text: This was furor Diabolicus; but what may not the devil do with his drudges, when God’s word cannot obtain the smallest things of us?
paragraphs.anchor: And shed innocent blood, &c.

paragraphs.text: Prompted thereunto by that old manslayer. This was practised by Manasseh, Ahaz, and others not a few, Jer 7:19 Eze 16:1-63 Haec atrocitas frequens apud gentes.
paragraphs.anchor: Whom they sacrificed unto the idols of Canaan

paragraphs.text: Impiata est abominabilis reddita est quasi hypocrita. See Ezr 9:11. As a hypocrite is a fair professor, but a foul sinner, so here.
paragraphs.anchor: And the land was polluted with blood

paragraphs.text: Great sins do greatly pollute; neither are men by anything more disadvantaged than by doting upon their own devices.
paragraphs.anchor: Thus were they defiled

paragraphs.text: They followed it earnestly, and with delight.
paragraphs.anchor: And went a whoring

paragraphs.text: Sin doth as naturally draw and suck judgments to it as the loadstone doth iron, or turpentine fire.
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore was the wrath of the Lord kindled

paragraphs.text: This was the greatest of all miseries, and a piece of hell.
paragraphs.anchor: Insomuch that he abhorred his own inheritance

paragraphs.text: That they might suffer by them with whom they had sinned, and with whom, by compliance, they hoped to have ingratiated.
paragraphs.anchor: And he gave them into the hand of the heathen

paragraphs.text: Heb. they were bowed down, or humbled, who would not humble themselves under the mighty hand of God, that he might exalt them.
paragraphs.anchor: And they were brought into subjection

paragraphs.text: And as many times told them, Servati estis ut mihi servatis, I have, therefore, saved you that ye might serve me the better; Sed surdo fabulam, but they would not hearken.
paragraphs.anchor: Many times did he deliver them

paragraphs.text: η χαρις αλλαξαι την φυσιν ου δυναται (Theogn.).

See for proof hereof the whole Book of Judges, and take notice of God’s philanthropy, who heareth men’s afflictions, as he did Hagar’s, Gen 16:11, and is oft found of them that seek him not, Isa 65:1. See 2Ki 14:26-27.
paragraphs.anchor: Nevertheless he regarded their affliction

paragraphs.text: Heb. their shrill outcry; not for joy (as the word is mostly taken), but for grief.
paragraphs.anchor: When he heard their cry

paragraphs.text: Which could not be vacated or abolished by the wickedness of men, but stood firm and inviolable, inasmuch as God is faithful and merciful.
paragraphs.anchor: And he remembered for them his covenant

paragraphs.text: That is, changed his severity into clemency. God’s repentance is not a change of his will, but of his work, Mutatio rei, non Dei.
paragraphs.anchor: And repented

paragraphs.text: God can soon turn the hearts of tyrants, and make them of lions lambs, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: He made them also to be pitied

paragraphs.text: This is the main request of the psalm, and the chief thing intended; for for this cause prefaced the prophet, as Psa 106:1-2, &c., and reckoned up the people’s sins and God’s deliverances, that he might bring in this, "Save us," as thou ever hast done.
paragraphs.anchor: Save us, O Lord our God

paragraphs.text: Good ends propounded in prayer is a special means of speeding. Hypocrites do all in themselves, so do not the saints, Hos 14:8; and all for themselves, as Zec 7:5 Hos 10:1, which is not the saints’ practice, Son 5:1, they have good aims in their good actions.
paragraphs.anchor: To give thanks unto thy holy name

paragraphs.text: viz. For our return out of captivity, which we foresee, believe, and give thanks for beforehand.
paragraphs.anchor: Blessed be the Lord

paragraphs.text: Thus they speak one to another, by way of excitation, υμνησατε μετα μελους το ον, so Justin Martyr rendereth it.
paragraphs.anchor: Praise ye the Lord
